changes.headline: Escalation premium unwinds on reserve-release talks
changes.dek: Brent ~$99.9 (-2.4%), WTI ~$89.5 (-3.6%) mid-session Friday. Friday's crude rally unwound on reserve-release talks: the U.S. president said Thursday the U.S. 'may ask' European countries to release diesel from emergency stockpiles, and EU governments discussed a French proposal Friday for 50 million barrels of European diesel plus 50 million barrels of IEA crude. European gasoil fell ~5% to $1,380.50/MT. Brent traded down to ~$99.9 (-2.4%) and WTI to ~$89.5 (-3.6%) by mid-session Friday (economies.com, ~06:00 MDT), after Thursday closes of $102.31 and $92.87; both headed for weekly declines (Brent -4.1% w/w, WTI -3.2% w/w). Gulf crude exports are at 98% of pre-war levels (JPMorgan) and Hormuz crude is back at 13.5 Mb/d on a seven-day average (Kpler): the flat-price rally was about escalation optionality, not missing barrels, and Friday took some of that optionality back.
changes.balance_read: Flat price trades the war headlines; a policy headline unwound the premium as fast as escalation built it.

changes.headline: WCS front widens again, into both rally and selloff
changes.dek: TMW Nov26 -$24.13 (-$0.38); Dec26 -$24.65 (-$0.40, widest on strip). ICE EOD Oct 2: WCS at Hardisty (TMW) Nov26 -$24.13 (-$0.38 on the day), Dec26 -$24.65 (-$0.40, the widest tenor on the strip), Jan27 -$23.30, tightening down the strip to Oct27 -$17.20; the whole strip sold off $0.1-0.7. WCS at Houston (ARV) Nov26 -$14.86 (-$0.31): the Houston-Hardisty arb widened to +$9.28 from +$9.21, so the constraint sits at the egress end, not the Gulf demand end. MSW (TMR) Nov26 -$0.91, giving back most of Thursday's tightening; UHC (TMU) +$3.40; condensate (TMF) +$3.85 holding into diluent season; synthetic (TMS) +$5.98, SYN-minus-WCS $30.11. WCS Nov outright ~$65.4, down ~$3.7 from Thursday, with the diff contributing this time.
changes.balance_read: The diff kept widening into Thursday's crude rally AND Friday's selloff: this is the November-December physical egress crunch trading through flat-price noise, not a structural repricing of Canadian heavy.
changes.publishers: ICE Report Center end-of-day settlements, Oct 2, 2026 (all six contracts)

changes.headline: Diesel $100+ regime breaks at $97.94
changes.dek: NYMEX diesel crack $97.94 (Oct 2): first sub-$100 close after eighteen straight above. The NYMEX diesel crack closed at $97.94 on Oct 2, the first sub-$100 close after eighteen straight days above $100. The 3-2-1 crack stands at $64.65 against a $75.31 maximum (Aug 28); maxima validated against the refreshed history (diesel $117.92 on Sep 16; 3-2-1 $75.31 on Aug 28). The break came with European gasoil -5% on the reserve-release talks: a policy headline unwinding a physical premium. Underneath, the physical tightness is intact: Russia's diesel export ban runs through October 31, Ukraine struck the Volgograd Lukoil refinery and the Samara oil distribution station overnight Oct 1-2, and China's October product-export cancellations stand.
changes.balance_read: Crude flow and product availability are not the same market, and Friday proved it in reverse: the policy headline that moved was a diesel-reserve proposal, and gasoil (-5%) moved twice as much as crude (-2.4%).
changes.publishers: Validated crack history (Yahoo front-month futures), refreshed Oct 3, 2026

changes.headline: Two tankers struck near Hormuz; barrels still flowing
changes.dek: UKMTO Oct 2: two crude tankers hit by unidentified projectiles near the Strait. UKMTO reported Oct 2 that two oil tankers were struck by unidentified projectiles near the Strait of Hormuz. The first, exiting the strait, took 'a small fire and blackout onboard'; the fire was extinguished, no casualties, and the vessel resumed its journey. Hours later a second crude tanker was struck east of Oman; crew safe, no environmental damage (AFP, Oct 3). On the U.S. side: the Roosevelt strike group and the Makin Island amphibious force carrying ~2,000 Marines departed San Diego, full deployment by November; Patriot batteries to Saudi Arabia and Qatar; new sanctions on Iran's auto and rail sectors. Against that: Iran confirmed receipt of the U.S. response to its ceasefire proposal via Qatar (under review), and the Saudi East-West pipeline restarted Sep 29.
changes.balance_read: The tankers keep getting hit and the barrels keep flowing: Gulf exports at 98% of pre-war, Hormuz at pre-war rates. That is the whole market.
changes.publishers: UKMTO incident reports via AFP; Al Jazeera live, Oct 2-3, 2026

changes.headline: Pacific Link designated first project of national interest
changes.dek: Pacific Link (~1 Mb/d) designated Oct 1 under the Building Canada Act. The proposed Pacific Link pipeline (~1 Mb/d, Bruderheim, Alta. to a port near Delta, B.C.) was designated October 1 as the first project of national interest under the Building Canada Act (Canadian Press; pm.gc.ca). Estimated $35.2-43.7B; federal and Alberta governments 45% each, Pembina 10% (option to 20%), minimum 10% Indigenous ownership via loan guarantees; conditions to be finalized by September 1, 2027. Near-term capacity: Trans Mountain's drag-reducing-agent project adds about 90 kb/d from January 2027 (in service January 2027 per Trans Mountain's Sep 2026 CER application); the broader optimization program targets 1.19 Mb/d by end-2028. October Mainline apportionment stands at 8% on lights and 4% on heavies (Enbridge notice, Sep 16).
changes.balance_read: Long-dated and prompt-neutral, but it changes the 2028+ egress math; the November-December crunch trades on the apportionment notice, not on Pacific Link (TMX DRA's +~90 kb/d arrives January 2027).

changes.headline: Positioning washed: Brent net long -84k to window low
changes.dek: Managed-money Brent net long -84k w/w to +63,651 (low of window). The Brent managed-money net long washed 84k in the week to September 29, now +63,651, the low of the window. The next bullish shock meets a lighter spec book, and the next bearish headline has less long to flush.
changes.balance_read: Positioning is cleaned out; price action from here is more about fresh headlines than long liquidation.
